feast of all saints – 01st november & the month of remembrance: from my own experience of having loved ones die, as well as what others have shared with me, i have found that usually, a fter a time, we sense that our deceased loved ones no longer need us to pray for them. now they just want us to connect with them in remembra nce of holy mass, visits to the cemeteries, and for any holy soul that may need our prayerful remembrance in november or any time of the year. praying and remembering them gives us a lovely and comforting presence. today’s feast calls to mind women and men who are known to us pe rhaps, who really embody these ideals, and who are taught by the spirit to learn from the wisdom of god. many of our brothers and sisters are been killed because of the faith as christians, like last week all the catholic christians that were murde red in the church in jordan. these are saints who have witnessed to their belief and faith, and now it has been taken from them like so m any in the past. they too, give us here in our parishes hope a nd courage, to be ambassadors for jesus, for truth, goodness, and love. we often take f or granted in the western world our freedom of religion etc., but not so in other parts of our world. god’s presence and response is always to fill us with his blessing, giving us a share in the very of the blessed one, so that if we perserve in friendship with god, we might ourselves become blessed, and join the company of the saints. november - reflection for the solemnity of all saints today, the church celebrates the solemnity of all saints - not only the famous saints we know by name, but also the countless men and women from every nation, language, and race who lived quiet, faithful lives and now enjoy the presence of god. think of our great-grandparents who may have lived very good lives but were not canonised as saints by the church. the vision in the book of revelation in our first reading (apocalypse 7: 2-4,9-14) reminds us that heaven is not empty; it is filled with a great multitude who have washed their robes in the blood of the lamb. in other words, holiness is not a dream reserved for a few special people. it is the calling of every christian. the second reading from (1 john 3:1-3) tells us something even more beautiful: “ we are already children of god .” this means holiness begins now. it is not something we wait for until after death. it starts in our daily choices, in the way we speak, forgive, work, pray, and relate with others. to be a saint is simply to belong to god and to allow his grace to shape our lives. do you want to be a saint? don't wait till tomorrow, begin today to do good and strive towards holiness of life. the gospel (matthew 5:1-12) on the beatitudes gives us the path to attain this holiness. jesus says that the poor in spirit, the gentle, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, and those who hunger for justice are blessed. these are not just beautiful words; they are practical lessons for daily life. holiness i s lived when we choose honesty over lies, humility over pride, forgiveness over revenge, prayer over despair, and peace over conflict. the saints teach us that holiness is possible in ordinary life. it is possible in the home, in the workplace, in the classroom, in illness, in old age, and even in suffering. the saints were not perfect people; they were people who kept returning to god. they failed, repented, trusted, and persevered. today, let us ask for the grace to live like the saints: to be faithful in sm all things, generous in love, patient in trials, and hopeful in god’s promises. may this feast renew our desire for heaven and remind us that the road to glory is walked one day, one decision, and one act of love at a time. all saints, pray for us. longford (templemichael)

enter into the joys of your master" (mt 25:21). we need to pray to the saints, both the canonized and the uncanonized, asking them to pray on our behalf that we may live our lives in faithfulness like theirs, and so receive the same reward they are enjoying. november intentions: those who wish to have their deceased remembered in masses during november, please fill in the form available at each entrance & drop into the box provided in front of the altar.

to avoid disappointment! november: month of remembrance each year, our church in its wisdom, sets aside the month of november as an opportune time when we are asked to remember and pray for our departed loved ones. it begins with our celebration of the feast of all saints on sunday november 1st. this great feast is followed by all souls day on monday 2nd. of all the feast days we celebrate over the course of a year, these are the ones that resonate with each one of us, when we remember our own departed loved ones, whom we pray are now enjoying eternal rest. when we remember and pray for our loved ones, particularly in november, their personalities and stories live on. we all have our own individual ways of keeping their memories alive. for some it is visiting a family graveside to say a prayer or place fresh flowers. for others it will involve writing the names on a list of the dead and placing them in a box near the altar in each of our 4 churches. they are then prayed for at each mass that is celebrated. for others it may be lighting a candle placed in front of a photograph of their loved ones as they offer a silent prayer of thanksgiving. in our parish church of st. mary’s, we have placed our remembrance tree in the sanctuary. it contains the names of the 47 people who have died in our parish over the past year. the highlight of our remembrance for them will culminate with the celebration of our special mass of remembrance on friday 20th november at 8pm, in st. mary’s church, when we invite their families to come to honour and pray for them. carrick-on-shannon (kiltoghert)
